newsitem.title: USA: OMB's Raines ready to continue budget talks.
newsitem.headline: OMB's Raines ready to continue budget talks.

text.p: Office of Management and Budget Director Frank Raines said Wednesday talks with Republican and Democratic Budget Committee leaders will continue for one more session Thursday, and depending upon assessment of progress, may resume next week.

The Thursday session will cover international affairs, he told reporters at the conclusion of Wednesday's closed-door talks. A meeting pencilled in President Clinton's schedule for Friday with congressional leaders to discuss the budget is not expected to take place, Raines added.
"We made a little more progress today," he said.

Raines said the White House was sticking by its offer of an additional $18 billion in reductions in Medicare spending, which brought the total to $100 billion. "We believe that is a very good proposal and that is our proposal."
After Thursday's session, time will be given to reassess positions. No talks will be held Friday, Monday or Tuesday.
"We are determined to keep at it as long as progress is being made toward an agreement, and do whatever it takes," Raines added.

Sen. Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, the senior Democrat on the Budget Committee, said it was positive sign that no proposals have been rejected out of hand. "I think the important part is that there is no one throwing up their hands saying 'that is a reject'. We haven't run into that and I think that is a positive sign," he said.
